title: Top K Frequent Elements
summary: Count how many times each distinct integer occurs.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–100,000 integers in [−10,000, 10,000]. k is between 1 and the number of distinct values. There is a unique set of k winners, so a tie never crosses the selection boundary.
contractDetails.output-checking: Compare the set of values and require exactly k distinct integers.

statement: Count how many times each distinct integer occurs. Return the k distinct values with the highest counts, in any order. Equal counts are allowed within the answer.

examples.explanation: −4 occurs four times, and 8 occurs three times.
Both winners occur twice, ahead of 0.
There is only one distinct value.

constraints: 1–100,000 integers in [−10,000, 10,000]. k is between 1 and the number of distinct values. There is a unique set of k winners, so a tie never crosses the selection boundary.
hints: Conceptual: The rank depends on occurrence counts, regardless of the integer's magnitude.
Directional: After counting, use frequency as a bucket index. No frequency can exceed the input length.
Implementation: Walk the buckets from highest to lowest and collect values until you have k.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) expected time and O(n) auxiliary space. Count first, then use at most n frequency buckets instead of sorting the values by count.
